To see what device documentation establishes about DNP3 security, we sampled 99 catalogue entries of 5 IED vendors and read their public documents (Appendix~\ref{app:crawler}). Of the 32 entries whose documents name DNP3, the documented findings are 6 (DNP3 over TLS or IPsec documented); 1 (DNP3 authentication documented; encryption not established); 3 (Control-traffic encryption documented; DNP3 scope not established); 2 (External encryption documented; DNP3 scope not established); 1 (A specific DNP3 security feature explicitly unsupported). For the remaining 19, the retrieved documents establish no DNP3 security; this is unknown, not evidence of plaintext operation, and for 11 of them some linked documents sit behind a vendor sign-in and were not read. Capability, default and deployment are separate questions. A documented capability says nothing about whether it is enabled: the Micro870 Controllers documentation, for example, states that DNP3 Secure Authentication is disabled by default. Deployment we did not measure: these are counts of sampled catalogue entries, not of vendors, installed devices or network traffic.
